meta.name: Alcohol Intoxication with Vomiting — RSI for Airway Protection

history.hpi: Friends report patient was drinking heavily at a party and became progressively less responsive over the last hour. He vomited twice on the couch and is now not rousing to voice, only moaning to sternal rub. No witnessed trauma, no known drug use, friends deny any pills taken.
history.lastOralIntake: Alcohol (large quantity, unknown type) over the past 4-5 hours; last food unknown
history.events: Friends called 911 when they could not wake him and he vomited a second time

scene.dispatch: 29-year-old male, unresponsive, residence, party in progress
scene.location: Living room of a house, patient supine on a couch with vomitus on the cushions and floor
scene.safety: No hazards to crew; several intoxicated bystanders present but cooperative
scene.bystanders: Two friends present, report heavy drinking over several hours, deny witnessed trauma or other drug use
visualCues: Vomitus on couch cushions and floor near patient's head
Empty liquor bottles on coffee table
Patient supine, moaning only to sternal rub

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew finds a 29-year-old male supine on a couch, minimally responsive to painful stimuli, with vomitus visible near his head and slow, shallow respirations.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Partially obstructed by pooling secretions/vomitus, audible gurgling
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, skin cool and clammy
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws to pain only, no purposeful movement
otherFindings: Vomitus visible in and around mouth
Strong odor of alcohol on breath
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: (moans incomprehensibly to sternal rub, no words)

transitions.if: Positioned and suctioned for airway protection
transitions.condition: Crew immediately positions the patient in the recovery position, applies suction to clear vomitus, and attaches monitoring while assessing for a toxidrome.

phases.name: Positioned and suctioned for airway protection
phases.description: The patient is positioned to protect against aspiration, suctioned, placed on oxygen, and monitored while the crew recognizes a sedative-hypnotic toxidrome consistent with severe alcohol intoxication.
phases.triggerCondition: After the primary survey identifies airway compromise from pooling secretions and depressed mental status, the crew repositions the patient, suctions the airway, and applies continuous pulse oximetry and capnography monitoring while obtaining IV access.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Improved with suction and positioning, intermittent gurgling recurs
otherFindings: Continues to have episodic emesis despite positioning
No purposeful protective airway response noted

expectedActions.shortAction: Position in recovery position, suction airway to clear vomitus
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patient positioning can significantly impact respiratory mechanics... This can both improve the ability to ventilate and limit aspiration. Suction airway: for significantly contaminated airways, consider utilizing a suction assisted laryngeal airway decontamination (SALAD) technique
expectedActions.rationale: Active vomiting with depressed mental status is a high aspiration risk that must be addressed before further airway management.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply continuous pulse oximetry and waveform capnography monitoring
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patients with significant respiratory distress should have continuous pulse oximetry and waveform capnography monitoring for both assessment and for guiding therapy
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes a baseline and trend for detecting respiratory decompensation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize sedative-hypnotic toxidrome; obtain IV access, check BGL
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Sedative Hypnotic: Central nervous system depression, Ataxia (unstable gait or balance), Slurred speech, Normal or depressed vital signs. Initiate IV access for infusion of treatment medication
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms the intoxication etiology and rules out hypoglycemia as a contributor to altered mental status.

transitions.condition: Despite positioning and suction, the patient continues to vomit with no protective airway reflexes and GCS remains critically low; the crew proceeds to RSI to secure a definitive airway.
The crew proceeds directly to intubation without having suction immediately available at the head of the bed, and the patient vomits during laryngoscopy.

phases.name: RSI performed for airway protection
phases.description: With protective airway reflexes lost and ongoing emesis risk, the crew performs rapid sequence intubation to secure a definitive airway.
phases.triggerCondition: The patient remains unresponsive with no gag or cough response and continued risk of aspiration; two airway-trained providers proceed with RSI per protocol after adequate preoxygenation.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Secured with endotracheal tube after RSI
otherFindings: Suction immediately available and used during laryngoscopy
ET tube placement confirmed with waveform capnography, bilateral breath sounds
Tube secured, depth noted at teeth

expectedActions.shortAction: Preoxygenate with high-flow O2 and positive pressure ventilation for ≥2 minutes before RSI
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patient should be pre-oxygenated with high flow oxygen, and positive pressure ventilation for a minimum of two minutes prior to the procedure
expectedActions.rationale: Adequate preoxygenation delays desaturation during the apneic period of RSI.

expectedActions.shortAction: Etomidate 20.5 mg IV (82 kg × 0.25 mg/kg = 20.5 mg) for induction
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer induction sedative agent: Etomidate IV push, 0.2-0.3 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Induces sedation to permit safe intubation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Rocuronium 82 mg IV (82 kg × 1 mg/kg = 82 mg) for paralysis
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer paralytic agent: Rocuronium IV push, 1 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Provides paralysis needed to optimize first-pass intubation success.

expectedActions.shortAction: Confirm tube placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds; secure tube
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Confirm placement of advanced airway (endotracheal tube, SGA) with waveform capnography (most reliable), absent gastric sounds, and bilateral breath sounds. Secure tube manually
expectedActions.rationale: Waveform capnography is the most reliable confirmation of correct tube placement.

transitions.condition: The airway is secured and confirmed; the crew maintains lung-protective ventilation and continuous capnography en route to the hospital.

phases.name: Ventilation and monitoring maintained
phases.description: The patient is intubated, sedated, and ventilated at an appropriate rate and volume, with continuous waveform capnography confirming ongoing correct tube placement en route.
phases.triggerCondition: After confirmed tube placement, the crew secures the airway and maintains protocol-directed ventilation with ongoing monitoring during transport.

otherFindings: No signs of tube displacement with movement

expectedActions.shortAction: Ventilate 10-12 breaths/min, 6-8 mL/kg tidal volume, target EtCO2 35-45 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Adult: 10–12 breaths/minute... Ventilate with just enough volume to see chest rise, approximately 6–8 mL/kg ideal body weight... maintain EtCO2 of no less than 35 and up to 40 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Lung-protective ventilation avoids barotrauma and hyperventilation-related complications.

phases.name: Intubation attempted without suction ready
phases.description: The crew proceeds to laryngoscopy without suction immediately available; the patient vomits during the attempt, and gastric contents are aspirated before the airway can be cleared.
phases.triggerCondition: Suction was not staged at the head of the bed before airway attempts; when the patient vomits mid-procedure, contents are aspirated into the airway, causing acute desaturation.

otherFindings: Visible vomitus in oropharynx during attempt
Coarse breath sounds bilaterally after event

expectedActions.shortAction: Immediately suction airway, consider SALAD technique, reoxygenate before re-attempting
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Suctioning to limit aspiration is a priority, since it is associated with development of hospital acquired pneumonia and related increases in ICU stay and mortality. Suction airway: for significantly contaminated airways, consider utilizing a suction assisted laryngeal airway decontamination (SALAD) technique
expectedActions.rationale: Immediate suctioning and reoxygenation are required to recover from an aspiration event before further airway attempts.
